title: FBR IRIS Portal: How to Register Your POS in Pakistan
metaDescription: A step-by-step guide to registering your POS on the FBR IRIS portal in Pakistan — what you need, how to get API credentials, and the errors that trip people up.
content:
What IRIS registration actually does

The FBR IRIS portal (iris.fbr.gov.pk) is the government system where you register your business and your point-of-sale terminals so they can report sales to the Federal Board of Revenue. Registering your POS is the step that turns "I have software" into "my sales legally reach FBR." Until your terminal is registered and its API credentials are live in your POS, every receipt you print is invisible to FBR.

The process is not complicated, but each step has to be completed in order — and the most expensive mistake is assuming you are done before the credentials are actually working.

What you need first

  • An active STRN (Sales Tax Registration Number) — confirm it is active on IRIS before anything else.
  • Your NTN and business details.
  • The number of terminals (points of sale) you will register.
  • Your IRIS login for iris.fbr.gov.pk.

The registration steps

  1. Log in to IRIS and confirm your STRN status is active.
  2. Open the POS registration section and enter your business address and terminal count.
  3. Register each terminal — one per active point of sale.
  4. Receive your API credentials (token/key) from FBR.
  5. Configure your POS with those credentials so it can submit invoices.
  6. Run test invoices and confirm they appear in your IRIS dashboard before going live.

Common registration errors

  • Inactive STRN — registration cannot complete until the STRN is active.
  • Billing before credentials are live — receipts print but nothing reaches FBR.
  • Unregistered new terminals — adding a counter or branch without registering it.
  • Skipping test invoices — going live without confirming submissions land in IRIS.

A real example

A retailer in Multan registered the business but forgot to register the second counter it opened a month later. Sales on that counter never reached FBR until a reconciliation caught the gap. Registering the terminal and re-submitting the backlog resolved it — but it was an avoidable scare.

After registration

Once your terminals are registered and tested, the ongoing job is staying compliant: reconcile monthly and keep the software current. See the full routine in our FBR compliance checklist, and if invoices stop landing in IRIS, the guide to common FBR POS issues covers token and sync problems.

faqs.question: What do I need before registering on the IRIS portal?
faqs.answer: An active STRN, your NTN, business details, and the number of POS terminals you plan to register. Have your login for iris.fbr.gov.pk ready; without an active STRN you cannot complete POS registration.

faqs.question: Where do I get the API credentials for my POS?
faqs.answer: After registering your terminals on the IRIS POS section, FBR issues API credentials (a token/key) that your POS software uses to submit invoices. Your POS vendor configures these so sales report automatically.

faqs.question: How many terminals should I register?
faqs.answer: Register one per active point of sale. If you add a counter or a new branch later, register its terminal before it starts trading — selling on an unregistered terminal is non-compliant.

faqs.question: What is the most common registration mistake?
faqs.answer: Starting to bill before the terminal is fully registered and the API credentials are live in the POS. The receipts print, but nothing reaches FBR until registration is complete.
